title: Kannada

how.d: Short, plain-English explanations — no grammar walls, no jargon without a translation.
Each phrase speaks in a native Kannada voice. Slow it to 0.2× and repeat until it sticks.
Every topic ends in practice: quiz yourself, then review the words until they stay.

hfaqs.a: No. Start with spoken Kannada in Roman letters, and let the script come second. Learners who speak first stay motivated far longer than learners who drill letters for a month before saying a word.
hfaqs.q: Must I learn the Kannada script before speaking?

hfaqs.a: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ for respect, ಹೌದು and ಇಲ್ಲ, ಧನ್ಯವಾದ, ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು, ಸರಿ, and ನಾನು — I. With those seven you can open any interaction in Karnataka politely while your vocabulary grows underneath.
hfaqs.q: Which words should I learn in week one?

hfaqs.a: The retroflex family new to most ears — ಳ, ಣ, long-short vowel pairs, rolled ರ. Ten minutes of daily listening retunes your ears within weeks; the pronunciation page walks you through each one.
hfaqs.q: What is the hardest part of Kannada?

topics.desc: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ opens every door in Karnataka — plus mornings, welcomes and warm goodbyes. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Yes, and nobody will mind — ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ with folded hands is understood and loved everywhere Kannada is spoken. With close friends a smile and ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ? (are you well?) feels warmer.
faqs.q: Can I just say namaskaara everywhere?

faqs.a: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ with folded hands and a small nod, and ನೀವು (neevu — formal you) until invited closer. Add ಅಣ್ಣ (anna) or ಅಕ್ಕ (akka) for someone slightly older — it warms everything instantly.
faqs.q: How do I greet an elder respectfully?

faqs.a: ಮತ್ತೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ (matte sigona — we'll meet again) is the warm standard. ಹೋಗಿ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ (hogi barteeni — I'll go and come back) is the classic respectful farewell — receive it with a smile and a nod.
faqs.q: How do Kannada people say goodbye?

topics.note: A note on ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ vs ಆರಾಮಿದ್ದೀರಾ. ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ? (chennaagiddeeraa) is the everyday are you well? — warm, quick, everywhere. ಆರಾಮಿದ್ದೀರಾ? is its relaxed elder cousin, heard over filter coffee. Start with ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ; the rest arrives with ajjis.
paras: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ (namaskaara) is the one greeting that never fails. Folded hands, a small nod, and it works with strangers, elders, shopkeepers and officials — exactly the people a learner meets first. Say it clearly, hold the folded hands half a second, and Karnataka opens to you.

Mornings get their own greeting: ಶುಭೋದಯ (shubhodaya — good morning), heard in offices, schools and darshinis until about eleven. Evenings soften to ಶುಭಸಂಜೆ (shubhasanje). Time-stamped greetings signal that you live in the language, not just visit it.

Welcomes are grand in Kannada culture: ಸ್ವಾಗತ (svaagata — welcome) opens homes, shops and hearts. Guests are greeted standing, often with water or coffee before a single question. Return the warmth — ಬಂದೆ, ಧನ್ಯವಾದ (I've come, thank you) — and you are family within minutes.

Goodbyes promise return, never end: ಮತ್ತೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ (we'll meet again) is the everyday farewell; ಜಾಗ್ರತೆ (jaagrate — take care) adds affection. Leave every conversation with a ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ and a smile — in Karnataka, how you leave is remembered longer than how you came.

topics.desc: Vowels, consonants, ottaksharas and the curly ಳ — the Kannada alphabet without tears. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Thirteen vowels (ಸ್ವರಗಳು) and thirty-four consonants (ವ್ಯಂಜನಗಳು) — 47+ letters that combine into ottaksharas. Sounds huge, behaves simply: learn the shapes and the combinations assemble themselves.
faqs.q: How many letters does Kannada have?

faqs.a: ಳ (lla) — the retroflex liquid, curled back: ಬೆಳಕು, ಕಳಸ. Then the ottaksharalu stacks — ಕ್ಷ, ಜ್ಞ, ತ್ರ. Listen, curl, practise: they arrive within weeks.
faqs.q: What is the hardest Kannada letter?

faqs.a: Yes — in writing: ಖ ಘ ಛ ಝ ಠ ಢ ಥ ಧ ಫ ಭ appear in Sanskrit loans (ಕ್ಷಮೆ, ಧರ್ಮ). Daily Kannada softens most of them; recognise them in print, relax in speech.
faqs.q: Does Kannada have kh, gh, bh sounds?

topics.note: A note on ಒತ್ತಕ್ಷರ (ottakshara). Kannada stacks consonants into ottaksharas: ಕ್ + ಷ = ಕ್ಷ, ಜ್ + ಞ = ಜ್ಞ. The second consonant tucks underneath the first — once you see the pattern, stacked letters read themselves. One look down, and the whole conjunct system clicks.
paras: Kannada vowels (ಸ್ವರಗಳು) come in thirteen: ಅ ಆ ಇ ಈ ಉ ಊ ಋ ಎ ಏ ಐ ಒ ಓ ಔ ಅಂ ಅಃ. Short and long pairs — ಅ/ಆ, ಇ/ಈ, ಉ/ಊ — change meaning completely: ಕಲ (kala — learn!) versus ಕಾಲ (kaala — time/leg). Length is meaning in Kannada; stretch with care.

Consonants (ವ್ಯಂಜನಗಳು) run five rows deep: ಕ ಖ ಗ ಘ ಙ, ಚ ಛ ಜ ಝ ಞ, ಟ ಠ ಡ ಢ ಣ, ತ ಥ ದ ಧ ನ, ಪ ಫ ಬ ಭ ಮ — plus ಯ ರ ಲ ವ ಶ ಷ ಸ ಹ ಳ. Round, curly, friendly — the script that looks like Telugu's twin and sounds like music.

Vowels and consonants marry into ಗುಣಿತಾಕ್ಷರಗಳು (gunitaksharas): ಕ್ + ಅ = ಕ (ka), ಕ್ + ಆ = ಕಾ (kaa). Learn the vowel-signs once and every consonant sings the same song — the system is vast but perfectly regular.

Then the crown jewels: ಳ (lla), the retroflex liquid — ಬೆಳಕು (light), ಕಳು (send); and ಣ (nna), the retroflex nasal — ಕಣ್ಣು (eye). Natives will grin when you land them; the grin is worth weeks of practice.

topics.desc: ಒಂದು ಎರಡು ಮೂರು to ನೂರು — plus clock time and market-ready counting. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: International digits for daily life — prices, phones, buses all use them. Kannada has traditional number words in full use (ಒಂದು, ಹತ್ತು, ನೂರು) but modern digits in print.
faqs.q: Kannada digits or international digits?

faqs.a: Take the number, add ಗಂಟೆ (gante — hour): ಮೂರು ಗಂಟೆ (three o'clock). Half past adds -ವರೆ: ಮೂರುವರೆ is half past three. One rule, every clock in Karnataka.
faqs.q: How do I say the time in Kannada?

faqs.a: ಎಷ್ಟು? (eshtu — how much?). Then listen for the number plus ರೂಪಾಯಿ (roopaayi — rupees). Market Kannada is the fastest teacher there is.
faqs.q: How do I ask the price?

topics.note: A note on ಒಂದೂವರೆ, ಎರಡೂವರೆ. Half hours glue -ವರೆ to the number: ಒಂದೂವರೆ (1:30), ಮೂರುವರೆ (3:30), ಐದೂವರೆ (5:30). Every language hides one clock trick; Kannada's is ವರೆ. Learn it and sound native instantly.
paras: One to ten: ಒಂದು (ondu), ಎರಡು (eradu), ಮೂರು (mooru), ನಾಲ್ಕು (naalku), ಐದು (aidu), ಆರು (aaru), ಏಳು (elu), ಎಂಟು (entu), ಒಂಬತ್ತು (ombattu), ಹತ್ತು (hattu). Chant them in rhythm — Kannada numbers love rhythm — and they stick in days, not weeks.

Eleven to nineteen build on ಹತ್ತು: ಹನ್ನೊಂದು (11), ಹನ್ನೆರಡು (12), ಹದಿಮೂರು (13)... then the tens march: ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು (20), ಮೂವತ್ತು (30), ನಲವತ್ತು (40), ಐವತ್ತು (50), ಅರವತ್ತು (60), ಎಪ್ಪತ್ತು (70), ಎಂಬತ್ತು (80), ತೊಂಬತ್ತು (90), ನೂರು (100). Past twenty, glue tens to units — ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂದು (21) — and count to a thousand (ಸಾವಿರ) without fear.

Money runs on numbers: the currency is the ರೂಪಾಯಿ (roopaayi — rupee), and ಎಷ್ಟು? (eshtu — how much?) is the most useful sentence in Karnataka. Listen for the number, repeat it back — ಐವತ್ತು? (fifty?) — and your first Kannada transaction completes itself.

Time reuses numbers with ಗಂಟೆ (gante — hour): ಎರಡು ಗಂಟೆ (two o'clock), ಐದು ಗಂಟೆ (five o'clock). ಈಗ ಟೈಮ್ ಎಷ್ಟು? (what time is it now?) is the question; half hours add -ವರೆ. Numbers, money, clocks: one skill, three daily victories.
topics.title: Counting in Kannada

topics.desc: Names, homes and small talk — your first real Kannada conversations, line by line. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ನಿಮ್ಮ ಹೆಸರು ಏನು? (nimma hesaru enu — what is your name?) for respect; ನಿನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು ಏನು? (ninna hesaru enu) for friends and children. Answer with ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು... (nanna hesaru — my name is...). Names first, always.
faqs.q: How do I ask someone's name?

faqs.a: ನೀವು ಎಲ್ಲಿಂದ ಬರುತ್ತೀರಿ? (where are you from?) — then answer for yourself: ನಾನು ... ಇಂದ ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ. Origin questions are the universal second question; prepare your answer before you need it.
faqs.q: How do I say where I'm from?

faqs.a: ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಮಾತಾಡಿ (please speak slowly) and ಮತ್ತೆ ಹೇಳಿ (please say it again). Said with a smile, these two sentences make every Kannada speaker slow down and help.
faqs.q: What do I say when people speak too fast?

topics.note: A note on ನೀವು, ನೀನು and ರೀ. Kannada has two yous where English has one: ನೀವು (neevu — formal/plural) and ನೀನು (neenu — familiar) — plus ರೀ (ree), the friendly respect-particle. Start with ನೀವು for every adult; let friendship invite you to ನೀನು.
paras: Every first conversation follows the same dance: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ, ನಿಮ್ಮ ಹೆಸರು ಏನು? (what is your name?), ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು... (my name is...), ನೀವು ಎಲ್ಲಿಂದ ಬರುತ್ತೀರಿ? (where are you from?). Four lines, and you have had a real conversation. Practise them in order until they flow without thinking.

Small talk runs on three questions: ನೀವು ಏನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತೀರಿ? (what do you do?), ಕನ್ನಡ ಮಾತಾಡ್ತೀರಾ? (do you speak Kannada?), ಊಟ ಮಾಡಿದ್ರಾ? (have you eaten? — asked with genuine care). Answer briefly, ask back immediately — ನೀವು? — because conversations are volleys, not speeches.

When the torrent comes — and Kannada hospitality pours words — deploy the brakes: ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಮಾತಾಡಿ (please speak slowly), ನನಗೆ ಅರ್ಥವಾಗಲಿಲ್ಲ (I didn't understand), ಮತ್ತೆ ಹೇಳಿ (please say it again). Every Kannada speaker honours these instantly; they are the learner's seatbelt.

Close warmly and promise return: ನಿಮ್ಮನ್ನು ಭೇಟಿಯಾಗಿದ್ದು ಸಂತೋಷ (pleased to meet you), ಮತ್ತೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ (we'll meet again). Leave with a ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ and the door stays open — Kannada conversations end the way they begin: with folded hands.
topics.title: Real Kannada conversation

topics.desc: ಹೋಗು, ಬಾ, ತಿನ್ನು — the twelve verbs that run daily life, plus how they bend. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Stems are orders to friends — ಹೋಗು! (go!), ಬಾ! (come!), ತಿನ್ನು! (eat!). Polite speech adds endings: ಹೋಗಿ (please go), ಬನ್ನಿ (please come). Learn stems first, politeness second, and never order a stranger.
faqs.q: Are verb stems commands?

faqs.a: ನಾನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ (I go), ನೀನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀಯ (you go), ಅವನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತಾನೆ (he goes). Person-markers on every verb — drill one verb through all persons and the pattern owns you.
faqs.q: How do Kannada verbs change?

faqs.a: ಇಲ್ಲ (illa — no/not) negates existence — ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ uses -ಇಲ್ಲ for verbs (I don't know). Kannada negation splits by word type; learn ಇಲ್ಲ for things, ಬೇಡ (beda — don't want) for refusals.
faqs.q: How do I say no to a verb?

topics.note: A note on ಬನ್ನಿ vs ಬಾ. ಬಾ (baa) orders a friend to come; ಬನ್ನಿ (banni) welcomes a guest like royalty. Same verb, different universe — the -ಇ ending is pure respect. When in doubt, add the respect: Kannada people forgive stiff politeness instantly and casual rudeness never.
paras: Twelve verbs carry daily life: ಹೋಗು (go), ಬಾ (come), ತಿನ್ನು (eat), ಕುಡಿ (drink), ಓದು (read/study), ಬರಿ (write), ಮಾಡು (do), ಮಾತಾಡು (speak), ಕೊಡು (give), ತೆಗೆದುಕೋ (take), ಇರು (be/stay), ನೋಡು (see). Memorise these stems and you can order food, find toilets, make friends and survive beautifully.

Stems bend by person in the present: ನಾನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ (I go), ನೀನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀಯ (you familiar go), ನೀವು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀರಿ (you formal go), ಅವನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತಾನೆ (he goes). The -ಉತ್ತ- (utta) infix marks present tense across nearly every verb — one infix, hundreds of verbs, instant sentences.

Polite commands add -ಇ: ಹೋಗಿ (please go), ಬನ್ನಿ (please come), ತಿನ್ನಿ (please eat), ಹೇಳಿ (please say). This one ending turns every order into an invitation — it is the most useful suffix in Kannada, worth more than a hundred nouns.

Negation and existence close the kit: ಇದೆ (ide — it is / there is) anchors locations — ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಮೇಜಿನ ಮೇಲೆ ಇದೆ (the book is on the table). ಇಲ್ಲ (illa — there isn't) removes — ಹಣ ಇಲ್ಲ (no money). Twelve verbs plus ಇದೆ/ಇಲ್ಲ: the engine room of Kannada.

topics.desc: Water, money, time, today — the everyday Kannada words that unlock daily life. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Time words first: ಇಂದು (today), ನಾಳೆ (tomorrow), ನಿನ್ನೆ (yesterday), ಈಗ (now). You will use them ten times a day — shopping, planning, chatting — while rare nouns gather dust.
faqs.q: Which words pay off fastest?

faqs.a: Kannada happily absorbs English — ಬಸ್ (bus), ಟಿಕೆಟ್ (ticket), ಆಫೀಸು (office). Use the pure Kannada word when you know it, the loanword when you don't. Fluency first, purity later.
faqs.q: Is mixing English okay?

faqs.a: Nouns first, verbs second, adjectives third. With fifty nouns and the twelve verbs from the verbs page, you can point, ask and survive — grammar glues them later.
faqs.q: Nouns or verbs first?

topics.note: A note on ಇಂದು, ನಾಳೆ, ನಿನ್ನೆ. Kannada time words pivot around today: ಇಂದು (indu — today), ನಾಳೆ (naale — tomorrow), ನಿನ್ನೆ (ninne — yesterday). Master this trio and half your daily sentences assemble themselves — ನಾಳೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ (see you tomorrow) alone is worth the lesson.
paras: Survival runs on nouns: ನೀರು (neeru — water), ಆಹಾರ (aahaara — food), ಮನೆ (mane — home), ಹಣ (hana — money), ಸಮಯ (samaya — time). Five words, and you can ask for water, find home, handle money and ask the time — the entire first day in a new city.

Movement words come next: ರಸ್ತೆ (raste — road), ಬಸ್ (bas — bus), ಅಂಗಡಿ (angadi — shop), ಶಾಲೆ (shaale — school). Karnataka moves by bus and foot; knowing ಬಸ್ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? (where is the bus stand?) saves more time than any app.

Opinions need adjectives: ಒಳ್ಳೆ (olle — good), ದೊಡ್ಡ (dodda — big), ಚಿಕ್ಕ (chikka — small), ಹೊಸ (hosa — new), ಹಳೆಯ (haleya — old). ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದು (olleyadu — that's good) approves everything from food to plans — the most useful single opinion in Kannada.

Weather and mood close the kit: ಮಳೆ (male — rain) matters half the year, ಬಿಸಿಲು (bisilu — sun/heat) the other half. ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತಿದೆ (rain is coming) starts conversations with strangers; in Karnataka, weather talk is friendship's front door.
topics.title: Core Kannada vocabulary

topics.desc: Dose, idli, bisibelebaat — order like a local, from breakfast to bill. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Point and say ಇದು ಒಂದು (idu ondu — one of these) — it works in every darshini, canteen and bakery in Karnataka. Add ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು (please) and a smile; grammar can wait until dessert.
faqs.q: How do I order with almost no Kannada?

faqs.a: ಖಾರ ಕಮ್ಮಿ (khaara kammi — less spicy, please). Kannada food honours chilli deeply; this one sentence saves sensitive stomachs while keeping every flavour.
faqs.q: How do I ask for less spicy food?

faqs.a: ರುಚಿಯಾಗಿದೆ (ruchiyaagide — it's delicious). Say it to the cook, the server, the ajji who packed your lunch — it is the highest compliment in Kannada food culture.
faqs.q: How do I praise the food?

topics.note: A note on ಬಿಸಿಬೇಳೆಬಾತ್. Bisibelebaat — hot lentil-rice, vegetables, ghee melting on top — is Karnataka on a plate. Order it at any darshini, mix with potato chips and boondi, and understand the state in one meal.
paras: Breakfast is the glory: ದೋಸೆ (dose — crisp crepe), ಇಡ್ಲಿ (idli — steamed cakes), ಪೂರಿ (poori — puffed bread), ವಡೆ (vade — savoury doughnut), all served with ಸಾಂಬಾರು (saambaaru) and ಚಟ್ನಿ (chutney). ಟಿಫಿನ್ ಮಾಡಿದ್ರಾ? (have you had tiffin?) is asked with love — answer honestly, then accept seconds.

Meals centre on ಊಟ (oota — the rice meal): ಅನ್ನ (anna — rice), ಸಾಂಬಾರು, ಸಾರು (saaru — pepper-tamarind soup), ಮೊಸರು (mosaru — curd), ಹಪ್ಪಳ (happala — crisp papad). Served on banana leaves at weddings, eaten with the right hand — ಊಟ ರೆಡೀನಾ? (is the meal ready?) is the happiest question.

Taste words steer every order: ಖಾರ (khaara — spicy), ಸಿಹಿ (sihi — sweet), ಹುಳಿ (huli — sour), ಉಪ್ಪು (uppu — salt). ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಉಪ್ಪು (a little salt), ಸಕ್ಕರೆ ಬೇಡ (no sugar) — with taste words, your plate obeys you.

Drinks and bills close the meal: ಕಾಫಿ (filter coffee), ಟೀ (tea), ಮಜ್ಜಿಗೆ (majjige — buttermilk), ಹಣ್ಣಿನ ರಸ (hannina rasa — juice). ಬಿಲ್ ಕೊಡಿ (please give the bill) ends it; ರುಚಿಯಾಗಿತ್ತು (it was delicious) guarantees a smile on your way out.

topics.desc: ಳ, ಶ-ಷ-ಸ, ottaksharas — every tricky Kannada sound, one by one, with examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ಶ (palatal, tongue high — ಶಾಲೆ), ಷ (retroflex, curled — ಕಷ್ಟ), ಸ (dental, on teeth — ಸಮಯ). Three s-sounds where English has one; Kannada ears hear all three instantly.
faqs.q: Why three different s sounds?

faqs.a: ಳ is retroflex — tongue curled back: ಬೆಳಕು (light), ಕಳುಹಿಸು (send). ಲ is dental — tongue on teeth. Say la-la sliding tongue back and feel the shift.
faqs.q: How do I make the ಳ sound?

faqs.a: Ottaksharas: ಕ್ಷ (ksha — ಕ್ಷಮೆ), ಜ್ಞ (jna — ಜ್ಞಾನ), ತ್ರ (tra). Pronounce each part quickly in sequence — k+sha, j+na. Ottaksharas look fierce and behave kindly.
faqs.q: What are those stacked letters?

topics.note: A note on ಳ (lla). Kannada's liquid signature: curl the tongue back WITHOUT touching the roof, and voice it — ಬೆಳಕು (light), ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ (silver), ಕಳೆ (weed). Children take years to perfect it, so forgive yourself months — then enjoy the applause.
paras: The three sibilants sort by tongue: ಶ (palatal — ಶಾಲೆ, school), ಷ (retroflex — ಕಷ್ಟ, difficulty), ಸ (dental — ಸಮಯ, time). Say sha-sha-sa sliding the tongue from high to curled to teeth — three letters, one glide.
The liquid ಳ curls back: ಬೆಳಕು (belaku — light), ಕಳುಹಿಸು (kaluhisu — send). Contrast ಲ (dental, tongue on teeth) with ಳ (retroflex, curled). Glide la-lla daily; the roof-touch becomes reflex.

Dental versus retroflex stops: ತ (teeth — ತಾಯಿ, mother) against ಟ (roof — ಕೋಟೆ, fort). Hold a finger to your lips: dentals puff forward, retroflexes pop upward. Ten minutes of ತ-ಟ alternation retunes the mouth within a week.

The rest behave kindly: ಚ is cha at word start (ಚಂದ) softening inside words, ರ rolls lightly (ಮರ), and long vowels simply hold double — ಆ, ಈ, ಊ. Kannada spelling mirrors speech faithfully: pronounce what you see, and you are right nine times in ten.

topics.desc: Verb last, respect built in — Kannada grammar in plain English, no jargon walls. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Put the verb last: ನಾನು ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಓದುತ್ತೇನೆ (I book read). Subject-Object-Verb, always. English instincts will fight you for a week; then SOV feels like home.
faqs.q: Where does the verb go?

faqs.a: ನನಗೆ (nanage — to me), ನಿನಗೆ (ninage — to you familiar), ನಿಮಗೆ (nimage — to you formal). ನನಗೆ ನೀರು ಬೇಕು (I want water) is literally to-me water is-wanted — Kannada wants flow toward people.
faqs.q: How do I say I want something?

faqs.a: ಇದು (idu — this, near me), ಅದು (adu — that, far). ಇದು ಏನು? (what is this?) points at anything within reach; mastery takes one shopping trip.

topics.note: A note on -ಗೆ (ge). Kannada's dative ending aims verbs at people and places: ನನಗೆ (to me), ಶಾಲೆಗೆ (to school), ಮನೆಗೆ (homeward). Sentences like ನನಗೆ ಅರ್ಥವಾಯಿತು (to-me it-is-understood = I understand) reveal Kannada's worldview: experiences come TO you.
paras: Kannada sentences end with the verb: ನಾನು ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಓದುತ್ತೇನೆ (I — book — read). Subject first, object middle, verb last — SOV, the order of half the world's languages. Rearrange your English instincts once, and every Kannada sentence parses cleanly.

Small endings do heavy work: -ಅಲ್ಲಿ (alli — in/on) places things — ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ (at home), ಮೇಜಿನ ಮೇಲೆ (on the table); -ಜೊತೆ (jote — with) joins company — ಸ್ನೇಹಿತನ ಜೊತೆ (with a friend); -ಗೆ (ge) aims motion and wanting — ಶಾಲೆಗೆ (to school), ನನಗೆ ಬೇಕು (I want). Endings, not word order, carry Kannada meaning.

Questions rise at the end: ನೀವು ಎಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀರಿ? (where are you going?) — ಎಲ್ಲಿ (where), ಏನು (what), ಯಾರು (who), ಏಕೆ (why), ಹೇಗೆ (how), ಯಾವಾಗ (when). Yes-no questions add -ಆ (-aa): ಊಟ ಮಾಡಿದ್ರಾ? (have you eaten?). Question words plus rising tone — asking is easy.

Negation splits three ways: ಇಲ್ಲ (illa) denies existence — ಹಣ ಇಲ್ಲ (no money); verb endings deny actions — ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (I don't know); ಬೇಡ (beda) refuses — ಸಕ್ಕರೆ ಬೇಡ (no sugar, thanks). Three no's for three jobs — Kannada refuses precisely.
